questions.question_text: If A stands for ÷, B for ×, C for +, and D for −, what is 46 A 2 C 21 D 8 B 3?
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If P represents +, R represents ×, S represents −, and T represents ÷, what is 5 R 9 P 7 S 9 T 3 P 6?
questions.explanation: Substitute the operations and apply multiplication and division first: 5×9+7−9÷3+6 = 45+7−3+6 = 55.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 9; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If P means ×, Q means ÷, R means +, and S means −, evaluate (fourth root of 81) R 6 P 3 S 26 R 64.
questions.explanation: The fourth root of 81 is 3. Thus 3+6×3−26+64 = 3+18−26+64 = 59.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If B means ×, C means +, A means ÷, and D means −, evaluate 11 B 22 C 288 A 18 D 50.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If B means ×, C means +, D means −, and A means ÷, evaluate 21 B 16 C 20 D 26 A 2.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 13; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If A denotes +, B denotes ×, C denotes −, and D denotes ÷, evaluate 34 A 15 B 3 C 11 B 2 A (51 D 17).
questions.explanation: Replace the symbols and evaluate parentheses first: 34+15×3−11×2+(51÷17) = 34+45−22+3 = 60.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 14; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If A means ÷, B means ×, C means +, and D means −, evaluate (87 A 29) B 14 D 24 C 14 C 6 B 5.
questions.explanation: Evaluate the parenthesized quotient first: (87÷29)×14−24+14+6×5 = 3×14−24+14+30 = 62.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In a code, a=0, b=1, c=2, d=3, e=4, f=5, g=6, h=7, i=8, and j=9. Treat each pair as a two-digit number. What is (cd+ef)×bc in ordinary numerals?
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 16; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In a code, a=0, b=1, c=2, d=3, e=4, f=5, g=6, h=7, i=8, and j=9. Evaluate (dc×f)−(bf−d)×d, then write the result using the same digit-to-letter code.
questions.explanation: dc=32, f=5, bf=15, and d=3. The value is 32×5−(15−3)×3=160−36=124; digits 1,2,4 encode as b,c,e, giving bce.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 17; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If 6×17 is written as 716 and 13×56 as 6531, how is 32×27 written using the same coding rule?
questions.explanation: Reverse 27 to get 72 and reverse 32 to get 23; concatenate in that order to obtain 7223. This rule also gives 71|6=716 and 65|31=6531 for the examples.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 18; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If 4−4=17, 6−6=37, and 2−2=5 under a defined pattern, what is 5−5?
questions.explanation: Each output is n²+1: 4²+1=17, 6²+1=37, 2²+1=5. Hence 5²+1=26.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 19; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If 9*7=32, 13*7=120, and 17*9=208 under the same rule, what is 19*11?
questions.explanation: The rule is the difference of squares: 9²−7²=32, 13²−7²=120, and 17²−9²=208. Thus 19²−11²=361−121=240.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 01 _.pdf, page 21; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If 2463=36 and 5552=30, then what is 6732?
questions.explanation: Apply the stated pattern: (6+7+3)×2=16×2=32. The examples agree: (2+4+6)×3=36 and (5+5+5)×2=30.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 4; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: If 5#6#7=9 and 6#9#5=10, then what is 7#3#6?
questions.explanation: The examples use half the sum: (5+6+7)÷2=9 and (6+9+5)÷2=10. Therefore (7+3+6)÷2=8.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 5; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Choose the correct sequence of mathematical symbols to balance 15 * 24 * 3 * 6 * 17.
questions.explanation: Option C gives 15+24÷3−6=17. By order of operations, the left side is 15+8−6=17; the other sequences do not produce equality.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 6; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Choose operations for the three question marks so that 33 ? 11 ? 3 ? 6 = 115, using each listed sequence in order. Which sequence works?
questions.explanation: For D, 33×11÷3−6=121−6=115. A gives 54, B gives 6, and C gives 26, so only D works.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 7; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Replace the three * signs in order so that 17 * 3 * 6 * 45 is a true equation. Which sequence works?
questions.explanation: Sequence D gives 17×3−6=45, and 51−6=45. The other sequences do not produce a true equality.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 8; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Choose operations for the five * signs in 18 * 14 * 6 * 16 * 4 * 254, in order, to make a true equation.
questions.explanation: A gives 18×14+6−16÷4=254, since 252+6−4=254. The other listed sequences either do not evaluate to 254 or place equality before the final value.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 9; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In 48 A 12 A 24 A 3 A 8 A 5 A 4, replace each A in order with the six signs of one option to make a true equation. Which option works?
questions.explanation: C yields 48−12+24÷3=8×5+4. The left side is 48−12+8=44; the right side is 40+4=44.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 10; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Choose operations for the five * signs in 221 * 17 * 3 * 60 * 7 * 10 to make a true equation.
questions.explanation: A gives 221÷17−3+60=7×10. Since 221÷17=13, the left side is 13−3+60=70 and the right side is 70; the alternatives are unequal.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 11; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Replace the six % signs in order with the operations from one option so that 35 % 4 % 12 % 3 % 6 % 5 % 5 is true.
questions.explanation: D gives 35−4+12÷3=6×5+5. The left side is 35−4+4=35 and the right side is 30+5=35.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 12; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Choose operations for the five * signs in 88 * 44 * 22 * 66 * 99 * 251 to make a true equation.
questions.explanation: D gives 88−44÷22+66+99=251. Division first gives 88−2+66+99=251.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 13; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Interchange + and × in both equations. Which equation(s) will not then be correct? I. 15+5÷1−9×4=70; II. 18×17+3−6÷2=133.
questions.explanation: After swapping, I becomes 15×5÷1−9+4=70, which is true. II becomes 18+17×3−6÷2=133, but its value is 66; only II is incorrect.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 14; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Interchange × with ÷ and also interchange 7 with 9. What are the resulting values of I and II? I. 8×3÷6+9−7; II. 9−7×1+6÷3.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 15; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: In both equations, interchange + and ×. Which equation(s) will not be correct afterward? I. 7−6+2÷1×9=2; II. 16+4−9×1÷3=60.
questions.explanation: I becomes 7−6×2÷1+9=4, not 2. II becomes 16×4−9+1÷3=166/3, not 60. Both are incorrect.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 16; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Which pair of signs should be interchanged in 20+5÷10×8−10=26 to make the equation correct?
questions.explanation: Interchanging − and + gives 20−5÷10×8+10. Multiplication/division first gives 20−4+10=26. The other pairs do not give 26.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 17; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Evaluate 108÷36×1/4 + 2/5×1/4 using standard order of operations.
questions.explanation: Multiplication and division are evaluated left to right: 108÷36×1/4=3/4 and 2/5×1/4=1/10. Their sum is 15/20+2/20=17/20.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 18; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Evaluate 100÷10−[−2+{−9+(3−6×2)}] using standard order of operations.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 19; exam/year not stated

questions.explanation: The numerator is 66−55+44−33+22=44. The denominator is 13×3+2×3−1=39+6−1=44, so the quotient is 1.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 20; exam/year not stated

questions.question_text: Evaluate 1/13 ÷ 1/13 ÷ 1/13 ÷ 1/13 from left to right.
questions.explanation: Division is left-associative: (1/13÷1/13)=1, then 1÷1/13=13, then 13÷1/13=169.
questions.source: Mathematical Operations 02_.pdf, page 21; exam/year not stated
